notes: The page's six question and example sentences ('When do you go to school?', 'I need to
sharpen this pencil') are excluded: they are phrases, not lexical items.
Dropped from the page at Leon's call: 'greenboard' (real but rare — a learner will meet
whiteboard or chalkboard instead) and 'examination' (the formal long form of exam, which
made a three-way near-synonym that fill-in-the-blank cannot grade unambiguously).
'clip' became 'paper clip': the page's Spanish is 'sujetador', and bare 'clip' is vague.
Two definitions are pinned because the English is ambiguous where the Spanish is not —
'compass' is the geometry instrument (compás), not the navigation one (brújula).
college/university (universidad) and grades/marks (notas) stay in one unit each: the
learner's difficulty is one Spanish word splitting into two English ones, so the unit is
built to be about the distinction.
Unit 6 holds all twelve subject names on purpose, so the learner sees why they belong
together. At twelve words it is the largest a unit may be, and the eleven-item session
cap means one subject will not get its own question — the match-up and the singles
between them still practise eleven of the twelve.

VERY_EASY: this is an A1/A2 course and these are its first pages. Difficulty sets the CEFR level and length of the intro paragraph, not the vocabulary — and it also sets what the unit pays in XP, so a harder unit later is worth more.

area.name: The School
area.description: El colegio por dentro: el salón y sus muebles, lo que llevas en el morral, los exámenes y las materias que estudias.

units.name: Places and people at school
units.topic: Where you study and who is there: the school itself, the places you go on to after it, and the people in a classroom

units.name: The classroom
units.topic: What is on the walls of a classroom and the furniture in it: the different kinds of board, the map, and where you sit

units.name: Things you write with
units.topic: What you write with and on: pens, pencils, what corrects a mistake, and the paper it goes on

units.name: Books, tools and your backpack
units.topic: What a student carries and the tools for measuring and drawing. 'compass' here is the geometry instrument for drawing circles, not the one that points north; 'paper clip' is the small metal clip that holds sheets together

units.name: The school day, tests and grades
units.topic: How the school day is marked and how work is judged: the bell, the words for an assessment, and the words for the result

units.name: School subjects
units.topic: The subjects on a school timetable, from the sciences and mathematics to the humanities, languages and beliefs
